title: ACDC structured Mirror transform
hypothesis: Two Mirror coefficients over shared ACDC diagonal basis factors preserve held-out operator quality with lower actual bytes and application compute than independent ACDC diagonal factors and dense matrices.
physical_object: fixed DCT-II transform and shared diagonal base factors at dimension 32
mirror_coordinate: two continuous coefficients per task selecting learned diagonal basis directions
logical_multiplicity: 64 task linear operators, including 16 held-out task identities

development.selection_metric: held-out nMSE, actual bytes, distinct functions, application MAC proxy

storage.authority: actual deterministic ZIP/NPY inference payload after reload

compute.proxy_definition: dense D^2 MAC/input; diagonal  D MAC/input; ACDC DCT FFT estimate 2*D*log2(D)+2D MAC/input

success_gate: Both dev seeds: Mirror held-out nMSE <=2e-4 and within 10% of independent ACDC; payload >=10% below independent ACDC and direct coefficient control; DCT MAC <=1.2x ACDC; 64 distinct maps.
failure_gate: Direct coefficient payload within 10%, quality gate missed, distinct map count <64, or compute >1.2x independent ACDC; fresh sealed.
boundaries: DCT convention deterministically reconstructible but transform compute charged
not trained ACDC or language-model evidence
